h: Mixing Bounces With York's Big Hitters
p: Rose Avenue sits on the west side of the city, not far from the railway lines that made York famous. That's handy, because one of the city's best family attractions is close by. The National Railway Museum, near York station, is free to get into and packed with locomotives, from historic steam engines to a Japanese bullet train. Kids can lose hours there, and it's a perfect calmer partner to a lively morning on the trampolines.

If you're driving in, York's park and ride sites are a sensible way to dodge city-centre parking, and the Poppleton site on the A59 is on this side of town. Once you're in the centre, the obvious favourites are all within walking distance: JORVIK Viking Centre for a whiff of tenth-century York, York's Chocolate Story for a sweet-toothed tour of the city's confectionery history, and a stroll along a section of the medieval walls for views over the rooftops.

A simple plan for a family day is to book a morning bounce, then head into the centre after lunch when the kids have burned off their fizz and are more likely to stand still for a museum. Teenagers might prefer it the other way round, saving the trampolines as a reward for a morning of sightseeing.

Whichever you choose, wear comfy clothes, bring water and keep a spare top handy, as sessions get warm. And don't try to cram too much in. York rewards a slower pace, ideally with a sticky bun somewhere along the way. If the weather's kind, the riverside paths along the Ouse are a gentle way to walk off lunch, and Museum Gardens near the centre has the ruins of St Mary's Abbey and plenty of room for small people to run about.
